turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr Brennan, you're in room two. I checked you just now, blood pressure 138 over 86, pulse 72, temperature 36.7, and your oxygen is 98 percent. Dr Keane won't be long.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, that is very kind of you. I shall wait here.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Declan, you're very welcome. Come on in and take a seat. What's been troubling you?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, thank you, doctor. It is my lower back. It has been sore for a few weeks, or perhaps since we moved house, and I could not say whether that was before Easter or after.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sure, we don't need the exact day. Tell me how it feels, in your own words.

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): It is a deep ache in the small of my back, about a six out of ten, travelling a little into the left buttock but no further down the leg. Lifting at the warehouse and sitting too long set it off, and lying flat or a hot water bottle eases it.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): I have that. Six out of ten, into the buttock only, worse with lifting and sitting, easier lying flat or with heat.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor, that is exactly it.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any numbness or pins and needles in the legs?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): The move was the difficult part, if I may say. We had boxes in every room, and I was up and down the stairs with the bookcases. My wife said I ought to have hired a van with a lift.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): That does sound heavy going. Coming back to the legs, though, any numbness or tingling at all?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. There is no numbness, and there are no pins and needles.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any weakness, or the leg giving way when you walk?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. The legs are strong, and I manage the stairs at work grand.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about the waterworks, any trouble passing urine, any leaking, or not getting there in time?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No, the waterworks are entirely normal, thank you.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the bowels, any change?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Normal as well. There has been no change.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you lost any weight?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Since the move my wife has been doing simpler dinners, as the new kitchen still is not right, and I have been picking at my food. Her sister said I looked thinner in the wedding photographs, though those are years old.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): I hear you. Have you yourself noticed a real loss of weight, or stood on the scales?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I would not say I have lost weight. The trousers fit just the same.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or turns of feeling hot and shivery?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister had a temperature last month and she was quite miserable with it, down in Galway. I brought her a carton of soup on the Sunday.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): That was good of you. And you yourself, any fever with this back pain?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have had no fever at all.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): What have you been taking for the pain?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol from the chemist, two of the 500 milligram tablets, three times a day, though I do forget the evening dose some nights. My wife is on metformin for her sugar and she offered me one, but I would not take another person's tablets. My sister swears by biotin for her hair, which is beside the point.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Quite right to leave the metformin and the biotin alone. So the paracetamol is yours, and you miss the odd evening one?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. Only the paracetamol is mine, and yes, I miss it now and again.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Roughly how many evenings in a week would you miss it, would you say?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, I could not be sure. Some weeks it is one night, some weeks more. I would not want to give you a wrong figure.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did you try anything else?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I was taking ibuprofen too. I thought it was a 400 milligram tablet, but actually it was the 200 milligram ones, two of them, twice a day. I stopped last week.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): What made you stop them?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): They brought on heartburn. That settled once I stopped, I am glad to say.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I know of, doctor.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any old trouble with the back, or any operations in the past?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never had an operation. There has been no previous back trouble either. I have been well, apart from this.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tell me a little about work and home. Do you smoke?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I work in the warehouse on the industrial estate, lifting stock, and it will be twenty years this autumn. I live with my wife. I have never smoked.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Grand. If you'll stand for me, I'll have a look at the back.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course, doctor.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): There's tenderness over the lower lumbar area, a little more on the left. Straight leg raise is clear on both sides, power in the legs is normal, and sensation is intact.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): That spot is precisely where it is sore, yes.

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): With a sore back a few things cross my mind, a muscle strain from the lifting, a disc being irritated, even the uncommon serious causes. I'm not going to conclude any of those today, and I certainly won't call this a slipped disc or sciatica.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): What I will say, as a working impression, is mechanical low back pain. Nothing in the story or the examination is ringing alarm bells.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Would an x-ray be wise, doctor, if you thought it proper?
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): I don't see a need for an x-ray today, and I won't be ordering one. If the pain starts down the leg, or you develop weakness, then we might arrange an MRI.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. I would be guided by you.

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep on with your own paracetamol, two 500 milligram tablets three times a day, and try not to skip the evening one. Given the heartburn, I won't start another anti-inflammatory.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stay on the move with short walks, and no lying up for days. The hot water bottle is fine. I'll refer you across to physiotherapy.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. Ought I to be careful with the lifting at work?

[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ease off the heaviest lifts for a fortnight if your supervisor will allow it, and bend the knees rather than the back. If you get numbness between the legs, trouble with the waterworks, weakness, or a fever, you come straight back the same day.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): I will, doctor. You have been very clear, and I am grateful.
[SEG0057] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it's no better in three weeks, book back in with me.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): I shall do that. Thank you for your time.
[SEG0059] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr Brennan, if that review needs booking I can take it at the desk on your way out. Mind the step there.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Much obliged. Good afternoon to you both.

spec.situation: Manual worker or office worker with low back pain for 'a few weeks or since the move'; doctor asks about red flags (numbness, bladder, weight loss, fever) one by one; patient answers some clearly, some vaguely or with a story. Painkiller use mentioned.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
